relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a GFAP variant carrier: "Next-generation sequencing revealed a pathogenic heterozygous missense mutation of the GFAP gene, p.Arg376Pro (c.1127G>C)".
method_note: Transcribed by hand from the text (no tables in the paper); JSON assembled with a short Python script in scratch. Scope: the proband plus two affected brothers (older brother: mental retardation, gait disturbance, suicide at 52; younger brother: mental retardation), described in the pedigree legend as 'suspicious relatives ... without genetic confirmation', so they have no variant rows and no disease label. Parents and three sisters 'exhibited no similar symptoms' and were not tested; as unaffected untested relatives they get no rows. 'He did not have any neurological symptoms' at presentation (age 51) is a time-bound broad statement contradicted by later symptoms; not recorded as an excluded feature. 'Notably, brain MRI did not reveal significant white matter lesions' (Discussion) is ambiguous between this patient and the ref [11] patients, so 'cerebral white matter abnormality' is left not reported; 'no areas of hyperintensity in the cerebral cortex' concerns cortex, not white matter. Age at diagnosis not stated explicitly (patient was 51 at presentation, when sequencing is described); left not reported. Age at last evaluation not stated (last events: tinnitus at 55, then follow-up 10 months later); left not reported. Inheritance not reported: no parental testing. Saccadic dysmetria, tandem gait impairment and macrosaccadic oscillations were not mapped to 'ataxia or cerebellar signs' because the paper does not call them ataxia or cerebellar signs for this patient. Normal Berg balance, caloric test and VEMP recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27). The variant was 'previously reported as a pathologic variant in AxD [4]', but the patient is not said to have been reported before, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null.
